rationale: JWT None Algorithm is a well-known, toolable bypass that can grant mass unauthorised flight clearances across the entire volume.
GNSS spoofing/jamming can redirect multiple UAS into restricted or manned airspace with potential for mid-air collision or ground impact.
SQL injection is a mature, scriptable attack; mass record corruption degrades operational integrity but safety impact is primarily indirect.
Poisoned weather or traffic feeds can push multiple UAS into unsafe routes or mutual conflict, but compromising third-party feeds requires upstream access.
Identity spoofing lets rogue operators authorise flights, but the blast radius is typically per-operator rather than system-wide.
C2 link loss during BVLOS directly causes fly-away or crash; MAVLink interception allows full command injection—catastrophic for any airframe in range.
Log tampering conceals prior attacks and destroys forensic evidence but does not itself cause immediate operational or physical harm.
Regulatory audit-trail compromise enables systemic impunity; safety degrades over time as violations go uncorrected, but direct physical harm is delayed.
Backdoored flight controllers give full aircraft control to the adversary; physical access or supply-chain compromise is hard but consequences are catastrophic.
Phantom tracks mask real conflicts and blind deconfliction services, directly enabling mid-air collisions across an entire service volume.
A single compromised vendor can backdoor an entire fleet; extremely hard to execute and detect, but impact is catastrophic and fleet-wide.
Poisoning the single source of truth cascades corrupted data to every dependent U-Space service simultaneously—maximum blast radius.
Physical sabotage of a vertiport endangers passengers and ground crew but impact is localised to one facility.
Spoofed altitude or IMU data feeds directly into flight-control loops, causing crashes as demonstrated by Asghari et al.
BMS manipulation mid-flight causes forced landing or crash; ground-station power loss halts all operations at that site.
API key abuse enables bulk exfiltration of sensitive flight-plan data; high reproducibility but safety consequence is limited to information disclosure.
Deleting no-fly zone boundaries via an unsecured API opens restricted airspace to UAS, risking collision with manned aircraft.
Strategic plan leakage aids adversary planning but does not directly endanger flight operations or physical safety.
DDoS against a single-point API gateway blacks out all flight authorisations across the volume; tools are cheap and widely available.
Injected fake geofence boundaries can silently reroute UAS into restricted or manned airspace, directly enabling catastrophic conflict.
Regulatory loopholes are persistently exploitable by any operator but erode safety standards gradually rather than causing immediate harm.
